title: BDK06 7-round AES-192 / aes192-7r-related-key-id-72bit-bdk2006

target.description: Shifted AES-192 interval, original rounds 2–8, with the preceding subkey and no final MixColumns. Explicit output is 72 mixed boundary-subkey bits, not a separately completed 192-bit master key.

setting.key_relation: Two structures of16 secret AES-192 keys each, inducing256 cross pairs. Across a pair the master-key XOR has DeltaK[3]=f and DeltaK[8]=DeltaK[12]=DeltaK[16]=DeltaK[20]=a, other bytes0. The attacker chooses nonzero a; f is varied by the structures, while b,c and for8r d are actual nonlinear schedule differences, handled as in Sections3.3/4.2.
setting.plaintext_model: Aggregate related-key chosen-plaintext queries under thirty-two structured keys; Section 3.3 gives 2^52 plaintext identities each under sixteen keys, while Section 4 gives per-key pools.
assumptions: Section 3.3 estimates 0.63 probability that the key structures contain a suitable pair. This is not automatically a numerical complete-key success probability.
Output widths count named selected-subkey values, not proved independent master-key bits. The remaining key-recovery completion is not priced.
This endpoint recovers 72 named subkey bits; other widths are not equivalent recovery goals.
The source conversion 2^6 memory accesses per encryption equivalent is an accounting convention, not a calibrated implementation measurement.

time.note: Author-reported native cost for this endpoint.

data.note: Aggregate chosen-plaintext calls over the thirty-two related keys, not per-key data.

memory.note: Source quantifies about 2^69 bytes for the seven-round algorithm and the detailed three-column eight-round endpoint.

preprocessing.note: Section 3.2 gives about 2^62 encryptions for known a,b,c,f; the final repeated unknown-difference setup is not separately repriced.

success.description: No separate numerical success is established for this72-bit named-subkey endpoint. The source0.63 statement models finding a suitable pair in the32-key structure; conditioned on it, small expected wrong lists are used to argue recovery. Pair incidence and wrong-candidate uniqueness are separate, with no independently quantified joint distribution. The source expectation is not converted into exact recovery success or complete192-bit master-key recovery.

components.description: Sections3.1–3.2: with the actual Table2 differences and correct boundary, the actual72-bit named tuple is not removed by the impossible-pattern test. This is conditional candidate retention, not a uniqueness or acquisition guarantee.
Section3.2 Step4 source24-bit pair-filter model. This records a pair fraction, not a count in one particular hash bin.
Section3.2 Step5c source conditional8-bit pair-filter model for one terminal-byte guess.

Section3.2 source uniform-elimination model: survival of ONE fixed wrong64-bit whitening guess after2^70 useful pairs. Multiplying by2^64 gives a source expected wrong-candidate count, approximatelyexp(-20), not a joint72-bit recovery probability.

Section3.3: two16-key structures induce256 cross pairs. This is the source approximately independent/uniform256-trial model for at least one suitable subkey-difference pair. Pair dependence is not independently proved, and this event does not quantify candidate uniqueness or output recovery.
